writeup.key_factor: Sunflower Showdown in Manhattan. Two clean anchor ratings with no compression artifact: Kansas State 1573 vs Kansas 1490 plus 18 home field gives the Wildcats a 64.1% win probability (fair -179) — the highest credible probability on today's board. Kansas arrives depleted (WR Kubecka and CB Gibbs out, ten players missed the Utah game) on a 17-game losing streak in this rivalry, while Kansas State is mostly healthy with QB Avery Johnson starting. Selected as Platinum under Growth Mode: highest model probability among the day's positive-EV plays in band; at the US retail price of -162 (FanDuel) the edge is +2.3 (it was +3.8 at the -152 exchange price in the morning scan).
writeup.risk: The edge is price-fragile: it only clears the classic +3% gate at -157 or better, and US retail has already moved to -162. Kansas State's No. 2 receiver TE Oakley is questionable and CB Patterson doubtful. Kickoff is 12:00 PM ET — this candidate expires if it is not approved and published before noon.

writeup.key_factor: The most defensible underdog edge of the day: two elite anchors — Indiana 1795 (No. 6 AP, 6-0) vs Ohio State 1829 (No. 1, 5-1) — and the model makes it nearly a coin flip in Bloomington (47.7%, fair +110) while BetRivers offers +133. External corroboration: SP+ projects it 26-26 (49% Indiana). The matchup supports the thesis: Indiana's pass rush is the Big Ten's best against an Ohio State offensive line with protection problems (11 sacks allowed) that is missing its starting right tackle (Siereveld, second straight game) and its RB2 (Jackson).
writeup.risk: It is still a play against the No. 1 team in the country: Ohio State's talent ceiling is the highest on the slate, and a 47.7% probability means this loses more often than it wins — the value is in the price, not the likelihood. Kickoff is 12:00 PM ET — this candidate expires if it is not approved and published before noon.

writeup.key_factor: Identical ratings (Air Force 1521, UNLV 1521) — the entire edge comes from home field at altitude in Colorado Springs, which the market is not charging the visiting Rebels for: Caesars still offers -102 while the model's fair price is -111 (52.6%). Selected under Growth Mode (probability-first, edge gate suspended for selection until mid-December) as the afternoon Gold: it is the only positive-EV afternoon play whose price survived the 10:30 AM re-verification, and its 3:30 PM ET kickoff keeps a live play on the card even if approval slips past noon.

Weather in Colorado Springs is under all veto thresholds (sunny, SSE wind ~10 mph), so there is no weather angle supporting or killing the play.

writeup.key_factor: ALCS Game 4, Cleveland up 2-1. Cleveland confirmed a bullpen game: Shawn Armstrong opens for 1-2 innings with rested bulk behind him, while Tampa Bay starts Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10 ERA, sixth in the AL, 13 scoreless innings vs Cleveland this year). Playoff-compressed Elo makes Tampa Bay 1556 vs Cleveland 1513 + 12 home field; rating Martinez a #2 starter (+20) and Cleveland's opener-plus-bulk committee at -20 gives Tampa Bay a 60.1% win probability (fair -151). Pinnacle's -106 implies only 51.5%. Even with both pitching tiers rated neutral, the model still gives 54.5% and a +3.1 edge.
writeup.risk: Weather is the main risk: rain most of the day in Cleveland with a playable window expected around first pitch, but sustained north wind near 21 mph with gusts over 30 mph, and a postponement would change the pitching matchup entirely (Tampa Bay could turn to Rasmussen on Saturday). Cleveland's bullpen has been elite this series (.152/.235/.235 against) and lefty Joey Cantillo is rested for bulk innings — if the committee performs like a frontline starter, the edge shrinks toward the neutral-tier +3.1 case. Tampa Bay is also hitting just .197 in these playoffs.
